title: Stretched VCF 9.0 architecture with back-in-time NSX convergence
prompt:
Build the production architecture artifact for the greenfield VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 deployment in `fixtures/greenfield.json` and the ordered migration plan for `fixtures/estate.json`. This is an architecture deliverable, not an explanatory report. Implement package `vcfarch`, expose `Build(scenarioPath, estatePath string) (Architecture, error)`, and produce deterministic `architecture.json`; the checked-in artifact and `Build` result for the shipped inputs must match.

Before implementing the design, research current Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, bill-of-materials, and upgrade-path sources for the component combinations and transitions involved. Record the sources consulted in `research/sources.json` as an object with a non-empty `sources` array. Each source must contain exactly `title`, `publisher`, `url`, `accessedAt`, and `decisions`: the first four values identify the source and its YYYY-MM-DD access date, while `decisions` is a non-empty array of the compatibility or upgrade decisions it informed. Each `url` must be an official HTTPS URL on `broadcom.com` or one of its subdomains. Cite those URLs in your final response.

`architecture.json` must contain `schemaVersion`, `greenfield`, and `existingEstate`. `greenfield.sddcSpec` must be an `SddcSpec` conforming to the SddcSpec schema in the VMware Cloud Foundation Installer API 9.0.0.0 contract. Use only the inventoried hosts and a supported 9.0.0.0 bill of materials. Assign all eight data hosts to the two specified site fault domains, keep the dedicated witness in the independent witness site and out of `sddcSpec.hostSpecs`, carry every requested network and infrastructure value, use the required stretched vSAN ESA topology, and calculate the per-site capacity and headroom proving that either data site can run the stated workload after loss of the other. Model the stretched-cluster topology and witness placement alongside `sddcSpec`, because the installer schema does not express them.

`existingEstate.migrationPlan` must validate against `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. Include every inventoried component exactly once, in strict contiguous execution order, with its inventory name, current version, supported target, method, and all required gates. The estate's NSX 4.2.1.3 build is newer than the NSX 4.2.1.0 build in its required VCF 5.2.1 convergence bundle: do not model that as a downgrade or ordinary upgrade. Preserve the supported skip-through-convergence disposition and then its forward lifecycle target. Also preserve management-plane-first/core-SDDC ordering, the fresh installation for the Logs transition, deferred NSX finalization, and witness-before-data-host sequencing.

Use only the Go standard library and keep `Build` safe for concurrent callers. Do not modify the fixtures, schemas, installer specification, license, verifier, tests, or `go.mod`. Run `python3 verify.py`.

research.subject: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 compatibility, interoperability, bill of materials, stretched-cluster witness placement, and the 5.2.1-to-9.0 upgrade path
research.verification_boundary: Verification checks the recorded source structure and official Broadcom HTTPS provenance without making network calls; the pinned compatibility snapshot is authoritative for the architecture artifact.
